injection_point.primary_why: this is the socket. Every closed-form detection number (R90 range solve, coverage C, EIRP/T_CPI ladders, ECA-depth sensitivity, phi sweep, wall map) reads the target sigma ONLY through this function. Replace its return value and you replace the target model and nothing else.
call_sites_in_primary: src/experiment_freespace_range.py:370 — sigma_d over the d grid (range solve)
injection_point.lookup_source: src/experiment_freespace_range.py:280 _sigma_lookup() reads outputs/report13_sigma_grid.json['sigma']['grid'][drone][band]['sigma_smooth_dbsm'] at line 288. Any replacement grid must supply that same key. ⚠ despite the name, at this grid that array is IDENTICAL to 'sigma_dbsm' — angular_smooth(win=3 deg, az_step=3 deg) has window n=1 and is the identity map (verified: allclose, max|delta| = 0.0). The pipeline injects an UNSMOOTHED pattern.
injection_point.physics_multiply: benchmark/link_budget.py:53 LinkBudget.echo_power_w(): num = eirp*grx*lam^2*sigma / ((4pi)^3 * R1^2 * R2^2). sigma enters LINEARLY, so a model swap is a pure dB offset on SNR at fixed geometry. Wrapped at src/freespace_link.py:299, consumed at src/freespace_link.py:469 inside snr_rd_db().

waveform_chain.amplitude: src/experiment_detection.py:150 — amp = sqrt(sigma_m2)*L/(sqrt(4pi)*R1*R2) inside build_echo_sionna(); the echo voltage is proportional to sqrt(sigma)
waveform_chain.note: the Monte-Carlo waveform chain injects ONE scalar sigma at ONE aspect, not a grid. Swapping the target model there means swapping that scalar; for M1 it additionally means deciding how often sigma_S is redrawn.

M1.model: 3GPP TR 38.901 §7.9.2.1 RCS model 1 — single scattering point (SPST) + statistical RCS
M1.channel_entry: H scales by sqrt(4*pi*sigma_M/lambda0^2) (eq 7.9.4-14, Step 15); sigma_D,sigma_S enter path power (eq 7.9.4-1, Step 10)

source.clause: 7.9.2.1 RCS of a sensing target — RCS model 1
source.size_from_calibration_table: 0.3 m x 0.4 m x 0.2 m (Table 7.9.6.1-1 / 7.9.6.2-1, 'UAV of small size')

table_7.9.6.1-1_and_7.9.6.2-1.Target type: UAV of small size (0.3m x 0.4m x 0.2m)
table_7.9.6.1-1_and_7.9.6.2-1.RCS for each scattering point: Component sigma_M: -12.81 dBsm; Component sigma_D: 0 dB; Component sigma_S: 3.74 dB for standard deviation
table_7.9.6.1-1_and_7.9.6.2-1.bistatic: The same values are used for monostatic RCS and bistatic RCS

verbatim_TR.text_model1: A first RCS model, called RCS model 1, is to characterize a ST as single SPST with component sigma_D of the monostatic RCS values fixed to 1. sigma_M is the mean of linear monostatic RCS values at the SPST.
verbatim_TR.text_sigma_FS: sigma_FS(theta_i,phi_i,theta_s,phi_s) is for the effect of forward scattering and is set to -inf.

corroboration_3gpp_ran1.why: the TR table value was agreed in RAN1; the agreement text uses the older component names A / B1 / B2
corroboration_3gpp_ran1.component_naming: A = sigma_M, B1 = sigma_D, B2 = sigma_S  (RCS = A*B1*B2)
corroboration_3gpp_ran1.quote_values: For mono-static, the following values of component A, B2 are agreed for UAV of small size. Component A: -12.81 dBsm. Component B1: 0 dB (already agreed in RAN1#118bis). Component B2: standard deviation: 3.74 dB
corroboration_3gpp_ran1.quote_model: RCS Option 3 is selected to model RCS of UAV with single scattering point for monostatic. B2 of UAV is modelled using log-normal distribution for monostatic. Different mean RCS values can be supported for UAV due to different size, shape, frequency, etc. For UAV of small size (option 2 for UAV size in UAV parameters table): B1=1, A is mean RCS value.
corroboration_3gpp_ran1.note: 'For mono-static' — the agreed number is a MONOSTATIC mean. The bistatic extension is the -3 sin(beta/2) term of eq 7.9.2-2, which the calibration table then drops.

secondary_literature_checked.NIST_5GNRad: github.com/usnistgov/5GNRad (Blandino, NIST CTL) — cited in OPENSOURCE.md line 23 and prior_work/outputs/prior_work.json tools[key=5gnrad] as the reference architecture h = h_bg + h_target with an injected RCS point target. It is an ARCHITECTURE precedent for the injection style, not a source of the -12.81 dBsm number.
secondary_literature_checked.Zhang_unified_RCS_2505.20673: searched the full 13-page PDF (BUPT, 3GPP-facing 'unified RCS' with measured DJI M350): the strings '12.81', '3.74', 'small size', 'model 1' appear 0 times. It does NOT corroborate the table value.
secondary_literature_checked.verdict: the primary source (TR 38.901 V19.4.0 §7.9.2.1 + Table 7.9.2.1-1) and the RAN1 agreement text are the only confirmations found. Nothing was guessed.

how_to_inject.closed_form: make _sigma_at() return the CONSTANT 10^(-12.81/10) = 0.05236 m^2 for every (az, el)
how_to_inject.bistatic: multiply by 10^(-3*sin(beta/2)/10); beta [deg] comes from freespace_scene.fs_params()['beta'] which the caller already has
how_to_inject.bistatic_caveat: TR 38.901 Table 7.9.6.2-1 (full calibration) instead states 'The same values are used for monostatic RCS and bistatic RCS', i.e. the calibration case DROPS the -3sin(beta/2) term. Run both: M1a (with) and M1b (without).
how_to_inject.statistical: sigma_S is drawn PER PATH in 3GPP. Our closed-form chain has no path ensemble, so the redraw rate is a protocol choice: (i) frozen at its mean (=1) for the deterministic curve, (ii) redrawn per CPI for a Swerling-like Pd. Declare which.
how_to_inject.waveform_chain: replace the scalar at src/experiment_detection.py:344 by sigma_M * sigma_S_draw

what_it_is_not: not aspect dependent — sigma_D == 1 in model 1, so the pattern is FLAT
not our airframe — 3GPP's 'UAV of small size' is 0.3 x 0.4 x 0.2 m
not a computed scattering result — it is an agreed table value
not frequency dependent — TR 38.901 gives one sigma_M for FR1 and FR2 alike

M2.model: metallic (PEC) cube, sigma computed with OUR kernel

provenance.paper: LowAlt-Cube — 'AI-Empowered Low-Altitude Economy: Cooperative Sensing With Fixed Wireless Access', arXiv:2605.07623v1 [eess.SP], 8 May 2026
provenance.exact_quote: The UAV is modeled as a metallic cube located at p = (x, y, 60), where x, y ~ U[-75, 75].  (p.8)
provenance.dimensions_search: the 13-page full text was searched for cube / side length / edge length / UAV size / dimension / '0.x m'. The cube's edge length is NEVER printed. Tab. I is the dataset split; the simulation-settings paragraph gives the BS/CPE counts and heights, 2.8 GHz, 20 MHz, 30 kHz SCS, Nc=512 — no target size. The words RCS and SNR appear 0 times in the paper.
provenance.our_choice: PEC cube of the SAME VOLUME as our airframe bounding box: a = (lx*ly*lz)^(1/3)
provenance.our_choice_why: the paper fixes no size, so whatever size we use is OURS, not theirs. Equal-bbox-volume is one declared scalar and makes the cube 'the same amount of object' as the airframe. It is NOT equal projected area and NOT equal max dimension — those rules give different cubes, all four are tabulated in targets.M2.size_rules.
provenance.scene_frequency_mismatch: the paper runs at 2.8 GHz / 20 MHz; we evaluate the cube on OUR three bands

M2.material: PEC, |Gamma| = 1 on all faces (the paper says 'metallic'). M3 is material-weighted, so normalisation (a) carries that asymmetry while (b) absorbs it — size in material_asymmetry
M2.kernel: rcs_sbr.rcs_sbr_batch — the SAME production function that made M3 (1-bounce SBR + PO surface integral, spacing = lambda/div, J^2 grid-phase jitter average), followed by the SAME n_f band average and the SAME 3 deg angular smoothing

kernel_crosscheck.interpretation: a convex PEC body has no self-occlusion, so first-hit SBR and all-faces PO must agree. The aspect-average agreeing (delta_mean_lin_db) is the meaningful check. The per-aspect residual lives in the coherent nulls, which are numerically fragile in BOTH kernels. NOTE: at this grid the declared 3 deg smoothing is a no-op (az step is also 3 deg), so the raw and smoothed residuals are identical — the nulls are NOT filled in.
kernel_crosscheck.null_caveat: the raw/smoothed RMS being equal is not a coincidence: angular_smooth(3 deg, 3 deg) = identity. Quote delta_mean_lin_db, not the per-aspect RMS.

M2.alternative_size_rules: equal_bbox_volume (CHOSEN) / equal_top_projected_area / equal_max_dimension / 3GPP small-UAV equal volume. They differ by several dB in sigma; the choice is declared, not derived.
what_it_is_not: not the paper's cube — the paper never gives a size
not a drone — it has 6 flat faces and 4 strong specular azimuths

kernel_plate_limit_check.test: pure-PO point-cloud kernel (rcs_po.rcs_from_points) on the a=0.34606 m cube at az=0, el=0 (face-on) vs the exact PO plate answer 4*pi*A^2/lambda^2, A = a^2
kernel_plate_limit_check.honest_caveat: rcs_po.py's own docstring says this test has ZERO diagnostic power for the kernel (at normal incidence P.u == 0, so the phase term vanishes and injected bugs still give +0.00 dB). It is quoted here only as an ABSOLUTE LEVEL sanity check — the kernel's real validation is the sphere test in rcs_po.validate() / rcs_sbr.validate().

M3.stale_warning: outputs/report13_sigma_grid.json was generated 2026-07-29 at git 4aa668b, BEFORE the 2026-07-31 mesh overhaul. Do NOT quote its absolute level. Its aspect pattern is also from the pre-overhaul meshes.
M3.stale_scope: this staleness enters ONE of the three branches directly (M3) and ONE indirectly (M2, whose edge length is derived from the CURRENT bbox while M3's pattern comes from the OLD mesh — see staleness.cube_edge_drift). M1 is untouched by it.
what_it_is_not: not measured — anchored only loosely; see docs/RETRACTION_LOG.md
not multistatic — the grid is monostatic sigma evaluated at the bisector

fairness_protocol.principle: only ONE thing may differ between the three branches: what the target scatters. Everything that is not the target model must be byte-identical.

held_fixed.why: if a branch bypasses the socket it also bypasses the out-of-range counter and the smoothing convention
M1 is flat so it is grid independent, but M2/M3 are not; a different grid changes their linear mean
sigma ~ 1/lambda^2 in the plate limit, so the band set alone can reorder the models
dB averaging would deepen the nulls of M2/M3 and leave flat M1 untouched — a silent bias

held_fixed.value: 3.0 deg power average, then INJECT THE SMOOTHED ARRAY
held_fixed.why: the consumer reads sigma_smooth_dbsm (line 288); injecting a raw array for one branch only is a rig
held_fixed.measured_fact: ⚠ at this grid the declared smoothing is a NO-OP: angular_smooth(win=3 deg, az_step=3 deg) gives n=1, and in outputs/report13_sigma_grid.json sigma_smooth_dbsm == sigma_dbsm exactly (allclose, max|delta| = 0.0). All three branches are therefore unsmoothed, which is SYMMETRIC and thus fair — but saying 'we smoothed by 3 deg' would be false. It matters here because M2's specular lobes are ~lambda/(2a) wide (a few degrees), i.e. exactly the scale a real 3 deg window would have flattened.

held_fixed.value: rcs_sbr.rcs_sbr_batch, spacing=lambda/16, jitter J=2 (J^2 offsets), 1 bounce
held_fixed.why: M2 and M3 must share the kernel so the comparison is SHAPE, not solver

held_fixed.value: unchanged: freespace_scene + freespace_link.snr_rd_db + the same snr90 threshold
held_fixed.why: sigma enters linearly at link_budget.py:53, so any detector change would confound a pure dB offset

held_fixed.value: all three evaluated at the BISECTOR aspect (that is what _sigma_at is fed)
held_fixed.why: M2/M3 grids are monostatic-at-bisector; giving M1 a real bistatic law while the others have none is a model difference, not a fairness violation — but it must be declared, hence M1a vs M1b
TR 38.901 7.9.2.2 defines a cross-pol matrix we do not use; ignoring it identically in all three branches keeps it out of the comparison

held_fixed.value: fixed; sigma_S draws (M1 only) use one declared seed
held_fixed.why: otherwise M1's 3.74 dB lognormal spread leaks into the difference as noise

what_must_NOT_be_matched: the aspect pattern itself — that is the object of study
the number of scattering points (M1 is 1 by definition; M2/M3 are surface integrals)

normalizations.name: none
normalizations.definition: each model keeps its own absolute level
normalizations.answers: if you had adopted this target model, what detection numbers would you have printed?
normalizations.danger: the answer is dominated by LEVEL. M2 in particular is not a drone-sized scatterer, so (a) mostly measures 'how big is the box you drew'.

normalizations.name: matched aspect-averaged sigma
normalizations.definition: scale each model by a scalar so all three share one aspect-averaged sigma (linear m^2 mean over the az x el grid); headline reference = M1's -12.81 dBsm
normalizations.answers: with the level argument removed, how much does the SHAPE of the aspect pattern change detection?
normalizations.why_this_reference: M1's level is an external published number, so referencing to it keeps our own stale absolute level out of the comparison entirely
normalizations.danger: a scalar match hides that M2's pattern has 4 huge specular azimuths; the mean is Jensen-optimistic for spiky patterns (linear mean >> median). Report median and p05 alongside.

normalizations.name: matched aspect-averaged sigma, reference = M3
normalizations.definition: same as (b) but referenced to our own grid
normalizations.answers: how do the other two look on OUR level scale?
normalizations.danger: ⚠ inherits the stale absolute level; do not quote as absolute

normalizations.name: matched aspect-averaged sigma, ONE scalar per drone shared across bands
normalizations.definition: scale each model by a single scalar per drone (from the band-grand linear mean) so the three share one overall level while each model KEEPS its own frequency slope
normalizations.answers: with the level argument removed but the band physics intact, does the illuminator-band ranking change?
normalizations.why_needed: normalisation (b) applied per band silently deletes the band slope, and M1's slope is exactly zero. If the headline is 'which band wins', (b) per band would rig it.
normalizations.danger: the shared scalar is a compromise: no single band is exactly matched

fairness_protocol.reporting_rule: report (a) and (b) SIDE BY SIDE for every headline number; use (b2) instead of (b) whenever the headline compares BANDS. If (a) and (b) disagree in ranking, the ranking is a statement about level, not about target modelling — say so in that sentence.
fairness_protocol.estimator_note: aspect average is the LINEAR (m^2) mean, matching src/experiment_freespace_sigma.py quote_policy ('m^2 linear mean, Jensen-optimistic, recorded'). Median and p05 are reported next to it because the linear mean of a spiky pattern is dominated by a few specular azimuths.

staleness.sigma_scale_hint_note: 40*log10(a_new/a_old) is the PO plate-limit scaling (sigma ~ a^4/lambda^2) — an ORDER OF MAGNITUDE hint for how much the cube branch moves with the mesh, NOT a measured drift of M3 itself
staleness.honest_statement: this experiment is a RELATIVE comparison between target models, so the staleness of our absolute sigma affects one branch (M3) directly. Under normalisation (b) referenced to M1 the level part of that staleness is removed and only the pattern part survives. Under normalisation (a) the M3 level is stale and must not be quoted as an absolute.

measured_drift.what: MEASURED, not asserted: the stale grid's el=0 row vs the SAME row recomputed on the CURRENT mesh with the identical protocol (n_f band average, div, jitter, materials, penetrate)
measured_drift.scope: el = 0.0 deg only, drones ['mavic4pro', 'mini5pro']. A full-grid regeneration was NOT run (hours of GPU, and benchmark/rcs_anchor.py currently owns GPU2).
measured_drift.how_to_read: drift_mean_lin_db is how much M3's LEVEL moved. Under normalisation (b) referenced to M1 that level drift is removed entirely. pattern_correlation_db (correlation of the dB patterns) says how much of the SHAPE survived — that part is NOT removed by (b).

material_asymmetry.why: M2 is PEC (the paper says 'metallic cube'); M3 is material-weighted with dielectric-shell penetration. Under normalisation (a) that |Gamma| difference rides along with the shape difference; under (b) it is absorbed into the scalar match. This number is its size.
material_asymmetry.caveat: measured on the CURRENT mesh at el=0 only, not on the stale grid

unknowns: LowAlt-Cube (arXiv:2605.07623) never prints the cube's edge length — searched the full 13-page text. Our equal-bbox-volume cube is OUR choice, not theirs.
LowAlt-Cube never prints the cube's material constants either (only the word 'metallic'); we assume PEC.

TR 38.901 gives sigma_M for 'UAV with small size' (0.3 x 0.4 x 0.2 m per the calibration tables) but never says which airframe that is, nor at which frequency it was derived — one number covers FR1 and FR2.
TR 38.901 Table 7.9.6.2-1 (calibration) drops the -3sin(beta/2) bistatic term while eq 7.9.2-2 keeps it; the TR does not reconcile them. Hence M1a / M1b.
The redraw rate of sigma_S in a closed-form (non-path-ensemble) chain is not defined by the TR — it is our choice.

outputs/report13_sigma_grid.json (M3) predates the 2026-07-31 mesh overhaul. The drift was MEASURED on the el=0 row only (staleness.measured_drift) — a full-grid regeneration was NOT run (hours of GPU, and benchmark/rcs_anchor.py currently owns GPU2). Rows at other elevations are unmeasured.
outputs/rcs_anchor.json and outputs/report13_sigma_grid.json absolute levels are stale — no absolute dBsm from our branch is quotable until they are regenerated.
M2 is PEC while M3 is material weighted; material_asymmetry measures that offset at el=0 on the CURRENT mesh only, not across the whole grid.
No detection run is performed here. This file defines the three models and the fairness protocol; the Pd / R90 comparison is the next step.
typhoonh480 and x500v2 are present in the sigma grid but were added after the 5-drone merge recorded in meta.drones_merged; they have no pre-overhaul bbox, so staleness.cube_edge_drift omits them.

stats_legend.mean_lin_dbsm: 10log10(mean of sigma in m^2) over the az x el grid — the estimator the pipeline quotes
stats_legend.jensen_gap_db: mean_lin_dbsm - mean_db_dbsm. A flat pattern gives 0; a spiky one gives a large gap. This is the number that says 'the linear mean is a few specular azimuths'.
stats_legend.top5pct_energy_frac: fraction of total sum(sigma) carried by the strongest 5% of aspects. 0.05 = perfectly flat (M1). Closer to 1 = a few spikes carry everything.
stats_legend.std_db: std of 10log10(sigma) across aspects — the aspect fluctuation that survives normalisation (b)

band_slope_db.meaning: aspect-mean sigma at the highest band minus the lowest band, per model
band_slope_db.why_it_matters: M1 is a single table value with NO frequency dependence (one sigma_M covers FR1 and FR2), so adopting M1 ERASES the band comparison entirely — every band-ranking headline would become a statement about waveform/occupancy alone. M2 and M3 both rise with frequency (plate limit sigma ~ A^2/lambda^2), but not by the same amount. Normalisation (b) removes the LEVEL offset but NOT this slope, because (b) matches one scalar per (drone, band).
band_slope_db.caveat: ⚠ under normalisation (b) applied PER BAND, the slope is removed too. If the study is about bands, match the scalar ONCE across all bands (per drone), not per band. Declare which.

ko: 세 모형의 자세평균 σ 는 서로 다른 세계에 있다 — 정규화 (a) 로 재면 순위는 사실상 '누가 더 큰 상자를 그렸나' 다.
M1 은 자세평균은 물론 **자세 패턴이 평평하다**(std 0 dB). M2·M3 는 안 그렇다 — 정규화 (b) 가 재는 것이 바로 이 차이다.
M2(정육면체)는 정반사 축 4개에 σ 가 몰려 std 가 M3 보다 크다. 자세평균이 같아도 검출은 달라진다.
⚠ 우리 σ(M3)는 낡았다(2026-07-29 격자, 07-31 메쉬 개편 이전). 정규화 (a) 의 M3 절대레벨은 인용 금지. 정규화 (b) 를 M1 기준으로 잡으면 그 낡음이 레벨로는 새지 않는다(패턴으로는 남는다).
⚠ M2 의 모서리 길이는 **현재** 메쉬 bbox 에서 나왔는데 M3 격자는 **옛** 메쉬에서 나왔다 — staleness.cube_edge_drift 에 그 어긋남을 수치로 적어 두었다.
⚠ 선언된 '3° 각도평활' 은 이 격자에서 항등이다(az 스텝이 3° 라 창 n=1). 세 갈래 모두 평활 없음이라 대칭이지만, '평활했다' 고 쓰면 거짓이다.
정규화 (b) 뒤에 남는 것은 jensen_gap_db 와 top5pct_energy_frac 이다 — M1 은 정의상 0/0.05, M2 는 정반사 축에 몰려 크고, M3 는 그 중간이다. 이 세 숫자가 '표적모형 선택이 검출에 무엇을 하는가' 다.

⭐ M1 은 **주파수 의존이 0** 이다(표값 하나가 FR1·FR2 를 다 덮는다). M1 을 채택하면 밴드 비교가 통째로 사라진다 — band_slope_db 참조. 그래서 정규화 (b) 를 밴드마다 따로 걸면 M2·M3 의 밴드 기울기까지 지워진다. 밴드가 주제면 b2_matched_per_drone_across_bands(드론당 스칼라 하나)를 써야 한다.

next_step.what_this_file_is: 세 표적모형의 정의 + 같은 축 위의 σ 수치 + 공정성 규약. 검출 실행은 없다.
how_to_run_the_comparison: 1) src/experiment_freespace_range.py 의 _sigma_at() 를 모형별로 갈아끼운다 (M1: 상수, M2: sigma['<drone>']['<band>']['M2_sigma_smooth_dbsm'] 조회, M3: 지금 격자)
2) 정규화 (a) 와 (b) 를 **둘 다** 돌린다. delta_db 는 normalizations.<drone>.<band>.b_matched_aspect_mean 에 있다
3) 헤드라인 수치(R90, coverage C, EIRP 사다리)를 (a)/(b) 나란히 보고한다
4) 순위가 (a) 와 (b) 에서 뒤집히면 그 순위는 레벨에 대한 진술이지 표적모형에 대한 진술이 아니다
next_step.cost_hint: σ 는 link_budget.py:53 에서 **선형**으로 들어가므로, 기하를 고정하면 모형 교체는 SNR 위의 순수 dB 오프셋이다 — 세 갈래를 다시 돌릴 필요 없이 오프셋으로 예측하고 한 번만 검증해도 된다.
